title: Ironwood Kitchen bowl-line launch package: neutralize eight mixed-light bowl shots to their in-frame grey card, deepen the flagship container band without a reshoot, vectorize the wordmark, data-merge one press-ready sell sheet per bowl, and cut the one 4K take to vertical + square + sizzle
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork recurring-role posting for a creative partner serving meal-prep / caterer businesses, whose listed deliverable scope was short-form video ads, vertical short-form / feed video content, product-showcase videos and video resizing / adaptation, plus the graphic-design line items paid social ads, website banners and assets, branding assets and promotional creatives, with turnaround weighted as the success metric. Laundered to a fictional meal-prep brand, 'Ironwood Kitchen' launching its High-Protein Bowl line — no real company, person, product, marketplace, software or trademark is named in any task-facing field (the real posting is not reproduced; craft-app and platform names in the original are described generically). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to raise the bar: the killed original amputated the photo work to a single hero still, padded the chain with four near-identical supplemental video clips fed into one quick-cut (an illegal multi-clip assembly), delegated the whole look to auto-tone + a temperature slider, and shipped only loose assets — the agent owned no designed artifact and could not really fail. The corrected design keeps the same job the posting rewards — one weekly multi-channel package for one launching meal-prep client — but routes it to what the connectors genuinely do and where the craft actually lives: the client hands over ONE continuous ~50s 4K product-showcase take of a bowl being assembled, a batch of eight raw product stills of the bowl lineup shot across two sessions under deliberately mismatched light (each carrying a photographic 18% grey card in frame), a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock, plus the copy roster and a genuinely hand-authored single-record page-layout data-merge template. The Adobe chain does the real work: neutralize all eight stills to their own in-frame grey card so the set reads as one white point, hold each bowl's true color, deepen the flagship's bright container band to a seasonal deep colorway without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, data-merge the authored template into one press-ready sell sheet per bowl (the agent-owned endpoint), and reframe the one take to a vertical + square social cut plus an AI sizzle. Nothing is invented beyond the deliverable types the posting already lists.
one_line_ask: Bring eight mixed-lighting meal-prep bowl stills to one consistent true-to-product look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries (deciding per frame how far and which way to move without killing any bowl's genuine color), deepen the flagship container's bright band to a seasonal deep colorway without reshooting, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record template against the roster into one press-ready sell sheet per bowl — and reframe the one 4K showcase take to a vertical and a square social cut plus an AI sizzle.
full_brief:
Ironwood Kitchen is launching its High-Protein Bowl line and needs this week's multi-channel package built off the assets we already have. We are NOT reshooting anything.

Here is what you are given: (1) ironwood_showcase_take_4k.mp4 — ONE continuous ~50 second 4K (3840x2160) product-showcase take of a signature bowl being assembled, steamed, sauced and pushed in on. (2) ironwood_bowl_photos_x8.zip — eight existing product stills of the eight bowls in the line. Here is the problem with them: they were shot over two sessions under different light, so straight out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble, and a launch set of mismatched shots reads cheap. To make the match checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. (3) ironwood_bowl_roster.csv — the copy for each bowl: name, SKU, description, case pack and price. (4) ironwood_linesheet_template.indd — the single-record sell-sheet page we hand-built, with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (the product photo and the masthead wordmark). (5) ironwood_wordmark_scan.png — our wordmark as a flat scan on off-white paper, which we want razor-sharp for the sheets and the container labels.

What we need back:
- THE SELL SHEETS (the main deliverable): a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, ONE single-page sell sheet per bowl, with the copy bound verbatim from the roster, that bowl's finished photo dropped into the product window, and our wordmark crisp in the masthead. One sheet per row of the roster.
- THE LOOK (this is the craft of it): bring every one of the eight bowl stills to a consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each photo was lit differently, so each needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target, and every dish must stay true to the product — once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point, with no bowl pushed off its real color. When you are done, hand back the white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set was matched to one target, not eyeballed frame by frame.
- THE SEASONAL VARIANT (no reshoot): on the flagship bowl shot, the meal-prep container's band is currently a bright red — give us a deeper, richer seasonal version of the SAME shot (a deep, slightly muted red in the same family, just deepened — not a jump to a different color), and the recolor has to sit under the band's real folds, sheen and shadow. No flat dead color, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the food and the table — just the band, with its highlights and shadow intact.
- THE WEB BANNER: from the finished flagship shot, a wide 16:9 website-banner still, cropped from the existing pixels (no added canvas, no fill).
- THE WORDMARK: our scan cleaned to a crisp vector for the sheet mastheads and the container labels — it must not look like a fuzzy scan when printed.
- THE SOCIAL CUTS: from the one 4K showcase take, a full-length vertical 9:16 (1080x1920) cut and a square 1:1 (1080x1080) cut for social — same runtime, reframed only, no trimming and no upscaling (the 4K master has the resolution for it) — plus a short AI highlight/sizzle version of the same take for the paid short-form ad, and a short scene/shot rundown of the take for the post caption and scheduling sheet.

Keep the sources in our Creative Cloud folder. Bind the names, descriptions, SKUs and prices verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our copy. Work to spec and fast; we measure this role on turnaround. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point with the per-frame moves reported; the band recolor natural under the existing light; the banner an honest crop of the flagship shot; the wordmark crisp vector; the vertical cut exactly 1080x1920 and the square exactly 1080x1080 at the take's full runtime; and exactly one press-ready sell sheet per roster row.

inputs.name: ironwood_showcase_take_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CAMERA ORIGINAL (declared at camera scale; no generative video model produces this length/resolution reliably, which is the point — it must be a real capture): a single continuous ~50 second 4K (3840x2160, 16:9, ~24-30fps) hand-held-steady food-studio take of a high-protein meal-prep chicken-and-rice bowl being assembled and presented in a clear meal-prep container with a coloured silicone band: hands portion grilled sliced chicken and fluffy rice, warm steam rises, a glossy sauce is drizzled, roasted broccoli and cherry tomatoes are added, then a slow push-in settles on the finished bowl on a light wood counter, bright clean food-studio lighting, shallow depth of field. Real food and hand textures, gentle real handheld drift, candid documentary product-video look, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions, no real brand names or logos on any container, packaging, clothing or surface (all packaging plain/unbranded).
inputs.realism_notes: ONE genuine ~50s 4K camera take, declared at camera scale so the video outputs are honest: a same-runtime 9:16 reframe holds >=1080 width from the 4K height (a 9:16 crop of 3840x2160 is ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is a downscale, never an upscale), a 1:1 reframe crops ~2160x2160 down to 1080x1080, and the ~50s runtime is comfortably longer than the ~15s sizzle so video_create_quick_cut only SHORTENS this one take (no assembly, no lengthen). The four near-identical supplemental clips from the killed original are removed — they only invited an illegal multi-clip quick-cut assembly and padded the count.

inputs.name: ironwood_bowl_photos_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of high-protein meal-prep bowls in clear containers on a light wood counter, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, roughly 4500x3000 before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot across two sessions under deliberately mismatched light: (1) HERO grilled chicken & rice bowl in a container with a BRIGHT RED silicone band, mixed warm window + room light, level (this frame is the flagship and the recolor target); (2) steak & sweet-potato bowl, cool bluish fluorescent cast, level; (3) salmon teriyaki bowl, warm tungsten cast, frame tilted ~3 deg; (4) turmeric chickpea bowl that is GENUINELY deep golden-yellow (turmeric/curry colour is the real dish), shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral — the warmth is the real food, not a white-balance error; (5) pesto chicken pasta bowl, warm window light, level; (6) southwest black-bean bowl, cool cast, frame tilted ~4 deg; (7) tofu veggie stir-fry bowl, flat and underexposed, level; (8) beef & broccoli bowl, slightly overexposed and warm, level. Every shot has real food texture, real steam, cluttered counter surroundings, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI, no real brand names or logos on any container/packaging/surface. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each.
inputs.realism_notes: ANSWER-KEY / diagnosis (do not surface in the brief): the eight frames need DIFFERENT, sometimes opposite corrections to reach one white point — warm the cool-cast frames (2 fluorescent, 6 cool), cool the warm-cast frames (3 tungsten, 5 warm window, 8 overexposed+warm), lift-and-add-contrast the flat underexposed frame (7), and recover highlights on the overexposed frame (8). Frame 4 is THE TRAP: the turmeric bowl is genuinely golden and its light was near-neutral, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral — the correct move is essentially no white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set); a naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real product colour. Frame 1 carries the bright-red container band for the masked seasonal recolor and is the flagship the web banner is cropped from. Frames 3 and 6 are tilted so they need straightening before grading. REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each crop fills the sell-sheet product window at ~300 DPI and the 16:9 banner by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: ironwood_bowl_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: product_name,sku,description,case_pack,wholesale_price,@image,@Wordmark and 8 rows, one per bowl in the line, in this order: 'Grilled Chicken & Brown Rice Power Bowl', 'Seared Steak & Roasted Sweet Potato Bowl', 'Teriyaki Glazed Salmon & Jasmine Rice Bowl', 'Turmeric Chickpea & Cauliflower Bowl', 'Basil Pesto Chicken & Orzo Bowl', 'Southwest Black Bean & Charred Corn Bowl', 'Sesame Tofu & Vegetable Stir-Fry Bowl', 'Korean-Style Beef & Broccoli Bowl'. Include at least one deliberately LONG product_name (e.g. the teriyaki salmon one, ~45+ chars) alongside shorter ones so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. description is a keyword-rich one-to-two-line menu/retail description of the dish per bowl (ingredients, macros, appeal) that names ONLY the food — it MUST NOT mention any lighting, colour cast, white-balance, exposure or grade direction, so the correction the agent applies stays its own decision from the grey card, never a value read off the CSV. sku is a code (e.g. IW-BWL-101). case_pack is a quantity string (e.g. 'Pack of 6'). wholesale_price is a US-dollar price (e.g. '$54.00 / pack'). @image names the finished photo file for that bowl (bowl_01_final.jpg ... bowl_08_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded photo into that row's single-record sheet. @Wordmark holds 'ironwood_wordmark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized masthead mark binds onto every sheet). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<product_name>>,<<sku>>,<<description>>,<<case_pack>>,<<wholesale_price>> and the two @image-path columns @image and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight sell sheets (page-count = row-count gate). The @image column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those EXACT names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned masthead lands on every sheet via a merge bind, never free-form placement. No 'type' column and no file-extension tell: all eight rows reference the same kind of asset (a .jpg the agent produces), so the CSV cannot telegraph which frame is the trap or which gets the recolor — that is the agent's to discover from the cards. Descriptions are client copy bound verbatim and are non-diagnostic (food only, never a cast/exposure hint).

inputs.name: ironwood_linesheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout data-merge document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait meal-prep sell sheet — ONE bowl per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<description>>, <<case_pack>>, <<wholesale_price>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @image (the finished bowl photo, a ~127 x 127 mm / 5 x 5 in window), and a masthead image frame at the top of the sheet bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The <<product_name>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long bowl name binds without going overset. The sheet furniture (rules, caption bar, page ground) is drawn into the template and fixed on every page, so the only per-row imagery is the product photo and the masthead wordmark. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd/.idml carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-bowl-per-page sell sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (eight rows => eight pages), not a multi-up catalog grid. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — that row's graded bowl photo AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every masthead without any free-form placement. Column names must exactly match the roster headers. The product window is sized so a ~127 mm square at 300 DPI needs ~1500 px of real image, which the ~4500 px camera stills clear by downscale only.

inputs.name: ironwood_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'IRONWOOD KITCHEN' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a bold modern sans-serif with a small flame-over-fork glyph, solid deep-charcoal letters. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), there is extra paper margin around the mark, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen. 2400x1400 PNG.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, generous margin, slightly soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper field and the soft edges if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: crop to the mark's tight bounds, boost contrast so the charcoal separates hard from the ground, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering. It is a SUPPLIED asset only vectorized, never a from-scratch designed letterform. Flat, limited-palette, hard-edged so the trace yields clean closed SVG paths suitable for the sheet masthead and screen-print container labels.

outputs.name: IronwoodKitchen_BowlLineSheets_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED DELIVERABLE. A press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter (8.5x11) portrait sell-sheet PDF, ONE bowl per page, EIGHT pages (page-count = roster row-count = 8), exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge. Each page binds its product_name/sku/description/case_pack/wholesale_price verbatim from the roster, drops that bowl's grey-card-neutralized, true-to-product photo into the ~127 x 127 mm product window (>=1500 px so it prints >=300 DPI) via @image, and drops the vectorized wordmark into the masthead via @Wordmark — both by merge bind, never free-form placement. The set reads as one matched look across all eight pages. The 'hero' is simply the flagship's page within the merged PDF (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the true-to-product colour, the crisp masthead — is the agent's, not a template default.

outputs.name: graded_bowl_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized bowl photos, delivered as BOTH the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized full-res masters (grey card still in frame — the neutrality-grading artifacts the harness keeps) AND the product-framed crops (bowl_01_final.jpg ... bowl_08_final.jpg, grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point, and every bowl's genuine colour held true (no bowl forced off its real colour); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered product crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by the per-frame applied-settings report (see grade_report.txt).

outputs.name: ironwood_hero_banner_16x9.png
outputs.spec: A wide 16:9 website-banner still cropped from the finished flagship bowl frame (grilled chicken bowl), ~2400 x 1350 px, an honest crop of the existing pixels of the ~4500 px-wide neutralized master — no added canvas, no fill, no upscaling. sRGB PNG for the web hero / feed banner.

outputs.name: variant_container_band_deep.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored variant of the flagship bowl shot: the bright-red container band deepened to the seasonal deep-red house colorway via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red — an in-band adjacent shift, NOT a near-complementary rotation) riding the band's existing luminosity, so its folds, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural and the food, container and table are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: showcase_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: A full-length 9:16 vertical (1080x1920) reframe of the whole ~50s 4K showcase take for the vertical short-form platform — SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe only, no trim), produced by video_resize [A]. The 4K height carries a 9:16 crop of ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. Frame-accurate cuts, captions and motion graphics are a separate in-house finish, not claimed here.

outputs.name: showcase_1x1.mp4
outputs.spec: A full-length 1:1 square (1080x1080) reframe of the same ~50s 4K take for the feed — SAME runtime, subject-aware reframe only, no trim, produced by video_resize [A]. The 4K frame crops ~2160x2160 down to 1080x1080 (honest downscale).

outputs.name: showcase_sizzle.mp4
outputs.spec: An AI highlight/sizzle cut (~15s target) SHORTENED from the single ~50s 4K showcase take for the paid short-form ad, via video_create_quick_cut [A] (the tool picks the beats). Shortens one longer take only — no assembly of multiple clips, no lengthening.

outputs.name: showcase_summary.txt
outputs.spec: A short scene/shot rundown of the showcase take (via media_summarize on the take) for the post caption and scheduling sheet.

outputs.name: ironwood_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat wordmark scan cleaned and vectorized to a crisp SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds, then a crisp contrast pass, then knock the off-white ground to transparency, then trace) — razor-sharp at any size for the sheet mastheads and the screen-print container labels, bound into every masthead via the @Wordmark column.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (NOT the primary output; the sell-sheet PDF is): for each of the eight bowl frames, the white-balance temperature and tint and the exposure/tone move that were applied, plus the final pixel size of each product crop, plus the single common white point all eight were matched to. This makes 'the set is matched to one target' checkable — the corrections must be non-identical across the differently-lit frames. It is an applied-settings log, never a measured/recovered pixel readout.

connector_workflow.note: Initialize a block upload of the single ~50s 4K take (media_type video/mp4) into the Ironwood Kitchen Creative Cloud project folder. Returns the transfer document + presigned block URLs. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.
Finalize the upload into a real CC video assetId with a fetchable URL — the single source for both social reframes, the sizzle and the summary.
Read the take's container metadata (duration, 3840x2160, frame rate) so the reframe targets and the sizzle length are set against the real span. Metadata read, not a pixel measurement.

Reframe the whole take to a clean full-frame 9:16 1080x1920 vertical for the short-form platform, SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe, no trim). The 4K height carries the 9:16 crop so 1080x1920 is a downscale, never an upscale. [A] async-widget. FINAL video deliverable.

Reframe the same take to a 1:1 1080x1080 square for the feed, SAME runtime (subject-aware reframe, no trim). The 4K frame downscales into the square honestly. [A] async-widget. FINAL video deliverable.

Produce a ~15s AI highlight/sizzle by SHORTENING the single ~50s take for the paid short-form ad (the tool picks the beats). One longer take in, a shorter cut out — no assembly, no lengthen. [A] async-widget. FINAL video deliverable.
Summarize the showcase take into a short scene/shot rundown for the post caption and scheduling sheet. Consumes the real AV take. FINAL data deliverable.

Neutralize the flagship bowl frame to its in-frame 18% grey card until the card reads a clean neutral (equal across channels) and set exposure/tone so it sits on the shared white point this set will hold. Reason the exact temperature/tint/exposure from THIS frame's card — do not reuse another frame's numbers — and report the move. Card RETAINED in frame: this is the neutrality-grading master, and it also feeds the recolor branch and the banner crop. Single primitive-built adjustments call (not a preset, not auto_tone).

Crop the neutralized flagship master to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet product window, framing on the bowl with the grey card cropped OUT, taken from the full ~4500 px master so it holds >=1500 px (clears 300 DPI in the window). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand, never upscale. Report final px. Uploaded later as bowl_01_final.jpg; card-neutrality is graded on the retained master (step 8), card-exclusion checked here.

From the same neutralized flagship master, crop a wide 16:9 website-banner still (~2400 x 1350 px), grey card cropped OUT, an honest crop of existing pixels only — no canvas extension, no fill, no upscale. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. FINAL banner deliverable.

On the neutralized flagship master, semantically select only the coloured silicone band on the meal-prep container ('the coloured silicone band around the meal-prep container'). Isolates the recolor to that part so the food, container body and table are untouched. Returns a maskURI. A real object, not a hue/coordinate selection.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes flagship master + band mask): keep the band in the red family but deepen it toward the seasonal deep-red colorway — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in red/wine; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a luminance drop that darkens the band, letting its existing luminosity carry the folds, sheen and shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the food and table) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the sheen) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the band lands on the rich seasonal deep-red target instead of a flat brick or a still-bright candy red, still riding the original luminosity so the sheen and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.
Resize the finished deep-red band variant to the same delivery frame as the set (grey card cropped out). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. FINAL variant deliverable.

Neutralize this bowl frame to its own in-frame grey card so the card reads neutral and the frame lands on the shared white point, holding the dish's true colour; set exposure/tone to match the set's brightness. Reason the correction from THIS card, distinct from the other frames' numbers. Report the move. Card retained (neutrality-grading master).
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_02_final.jpg.
Triage: this frame is tilted, so level it first (image_auto_straighten is the only tool that rectifies a tilt). Deciding which frames need this is part of the job — the level frames skip it.

Neutralize the straightened frame to its own in-frame grey card onto the shared white point, holding the dish's true colour and matching set brightness. Reason the correction from THIS card; the direction and amount are yours to judge from it, not the batch. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_03_final.jpg.

Neutralize this bowl frame by reading its OWN in-frame grey card: match it to the shared white point and set exposure to the set — but let the card decide how far to move, and hold the dish's genuine colour rather than chasing a look the batch expects. Do not reuse another frame's correction. Report the move (including WB held, if the card is already neutral). Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_04_final.jpg.

Neutralize this bowl frame to its own in-frame grey card onto the shared white point, holding true colour and matching set brightness. Reason the correction from THIS card, distinct numbers per frame. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_05_final.jpg.
Triage: this frame is tilted, so level it first before grading.

Neutralize the straightened frame to its own in-frame grey card onto the shared white point, holding true colour and matching set brightness. Reason the correction from THIS card. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_06_final.jpg.

Bring this bowl frame onto the shared look: the dominant work here is tonal (its exposure is off from the set) plus a white-balance decision read from its own in-frame grey card so the card lands neutral. Judge both from THIS frame, not the batch. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_07_final.jpg.

Bring this bowl frame onto the shared look: recover any clipped highlights first, then set a white-balance read from its own in-frame grey card so the card lands neutral on the shared white point. Judge from THIS frame; opposite tonal direction from the underexposed one is expected. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own retained card. Card retained.
Crop to the ~127 mm square sell-sheet window from the full master (>=1500 px), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. bowl_08_final.jpg.
Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the scan to the tight bounds of the mark (strips the paper margin) so the trace sees only the lettering and glyph, not empty paper.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the charcoal lettering separates hard-edged from the off-white ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.

Prep-before-trace step 3: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The mark is open-lettered on a light ground, so this is a clean outer-background knockout, not an enclosed-counter/dark-ground case.

Trace the prepared raster (cropped, crisped, transparent) into clean closed SVG paths for the sheet masthead and the screen-print container labels. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. Vectorize of a SUPPLIED, prepared flat mark — no letterform is designed. FINAL vector deliverable, and the @Wordmark asset the merge binds.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across four branches off the client's supplied assets. VIDEO SPINE: the one ~50s 4K take is uploaded (1) and finalized (2 -> take_asset); video_metadata (3) reads its span, then take_asset drives three same-runtime video outputs — video_resize to 9:16 (4) and to 1:1 (5), and video_create_quick_cut (6) which SHORTENS the single take to the ~15s sizzle (no assembly) — plus media_summarize (7) for the caption rundown. IMAGE SPINE: eight per-bowl grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per frame; distinct numbers each, all converging on one shared white point) followed by an image_crop_and_resize product crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames (17, 24) before their grade. The flagship's neutralized master (bowl1_neutralized, step 8) feeds THREE consumers: its sell-sheet crop (9), the 16:9 banner crop (10), and the recolor branch — image_select_by_prompt (11) -> masked image_adjust_hsl (12) -> masked image_adjust_hsl (13) -> resize (14), the two HSL passes both consuming band_mask. WORDMARK BRANCH: crop_to_bounds (31) -> crisp adjustments (32) -> remove_background to transparency (33) -> image_vectorize (34 -> ironwood_wordmark.svg). CONVERGENCE: the eight product crops (bowl_0N_final) and the wordmark SVG fan into the merge upload session (35) -> finalize (36 -> merge_asset_urns) -> document_merge_data_layout (37), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one sheet per row resolving BOTH @image and @Wordmark; the merged set is exported once by document_render_layout (38) to the per-bowl press PDF. The only non-chained calls are the two upload idioms (1, 35), each immediately consumed by its finalize; every other step sets inputs_from to a producing step's output, and no step's output is left unconsumed.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 38 connector calls, 16 distinct Adobe tools across four groups (video [A]/[C], image raster [C], asset storage [C], data-merge [T]/[C]) — well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the two upload idioms. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision, all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction or per-frame auto-tone (which keys off each frame's own histogram) visibly fails to match at the cards. Layered on top: a masked, luminosity-preserving container-band recolor (a within-family bright-red -> deep-red deepen, an in-band adjacent shift image_adjust_hsl can actually hold — no near-complementary rotation) executed as two HSL passes, with a written rationale for why color_overlay (whole-image) and fill_area (flat dead-fill) are both wrong; a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of an off-white, margin-padded, soft-edged scan; a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template; and same-runtime 9:16/1:1 reframes plus a legal single-take quick-cut off one 4K master. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch layout; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; video_resize is same-runtime reframe (no trim, no upscale) and video_create_quick_cut only shortens the ONE longer take (no multi-clip assembly, the killed original's defect); convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; the merge places one record per page (no N-up). Deprecated tools (image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast) are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; auto_tone appears only as the named trap.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every bowl still carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the set must read as ONE matched look — each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master, driven to one common white point — and because the eight frames were lit differently, each needs its OWN correction (some warmed, some cooled, one lifted, one highlight-recovered); running one global correction or per-frame auto-tone leaves the frames disagreeing at the cards and the set is rejected, and the agent must REPORT the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure move and final pixel size so 'matched' is auditable. Two further checkable gates: every product crop must clear >=1500 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the ~127 mm sell-sheet window, and the merged PDF page-count must equal the roster row-count (8), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable common white point across eight differently-lit stills, each requiring a different, sometimes opposite correction reasoned to its own retained grey card — not one set of sliders; (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving bright-red -> deep-red container-band recolor that must keep satin sheen and shadow natural using the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl), not color_overlay (whole-image) or fill_area (flat dead-fill) — an in-band deepen-and-mute, never a near-complementary rotation; plus prep-before-trace discipline on an off-white, margin-padded, soft scan (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAP (the brief does NOT disclose it — it states only the goal 'keep every bowl's genuine colour true' and leaves the method to the agent; the diagnosis lives only in the inputs' realism_notes): the Turmeric Chickpea bowl (frame 4) is genuinely deep golden and was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card is ALREADY neutral — the naive path batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' correction used on the fluorescent/cool frames, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', which pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real product colour; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. Secondary pitfalls the brief also does not telegraph: cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference — which is why neutrality is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing masters and card-exclusion checked separately on the crops); a multi-clip quick-cut assembly (only the one take may be shortened); tracing the raw scan; and running color_overlay/fill_area for the band recolor. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, agent never measures): every grey card neutral (per-channel spread near zero) at the common white point on the eight RETAINED masters with per-frame WB/exposure reported; every product crop >=1500 px with final px reported; the band recolored within its mask only; the banner an honest crop of existing pixels; the vertical cut exactly 1080x1920 and the square exactly 1080x1080 at the take's full runtime; the sizzle shorter than the take; the wordmark a crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter sheet per roster row.
